Reject a Written-Out Grid Where There Is No Path

Source: R/hyper.R
reject_pathless_values.Rd

Signals an error when the caller gave several values for a hyperparameter whose penalty has no kink.

Usage

reject_pathless_values(values, pen, what = "this term")

Arguments

values

The written-out grids, as check_values() returns them.

pen

The penalty the term will build, or NULL.

what

The term's label, for the message.

Value

NULL, invisibly.

Details

Several values are a grid for a path to visit, and only a penalty with a kink is swept along one: everything else has its hyperparameter read at the mode by a marginal criterion, which would take the vector and do nothing with it. The question is put to the penalty at a probe value of its own hyperparameters, the kink set being structural, so a ridge and a random effect under a Gaussian prior are covered by the same line as a family added later.

See also

check_values(), term_values()
